ai.description: Duttaphrynus kiphirensis is a small toad reaching 45 mm. It features a dark brown dorsum with scattered tubercles and a distinct, pale mid-dorsal stripe. It lacks cranial crests.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus kiphirensis* is best distinguished by its unique, prominent, and elongated parotoid glands that are significantly more slender than those of other Indian toads.
ai.habitat: *Duttaphrynus kiphirensis* is found in the high-altitude subtropical forests of Nagaland, India, typically inhabiting moist, dense vegetation at elevations around 1,500m.
ai.behavior: Duttaphrynus kiphirensis is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus kiphirensis* breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying eggs in long, gelatinous strings typical of the genus in shallow water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Duttaphrynus kiphirensis* is endemic to the Kiphire district of Nagaland in Northeast India, occurring at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Duttaphrynus kiphirensis* is a series of pulsed, high-pitched notes emitted from within dense, high-altitude forest vegetation.
